parsing_rationale: The document is a Quickstart Validation Guide for a Sales Item Management System. It describes manual validation scenarios for catalog display, search, sorting, CRUD operations, and persistence. I mapped these scenarios to functional requirements and success criteria, identified technical constraints from prerequisites, and declared missing standard spec sections as structural gaps.

project_info.brief_explanation: A vanilla JS web application for managing a sales item catalog with search, filtering, sorting, CRUD operations, and local persistence.
project_info.source_context: Quickstart Validation Guide extracted from a markdown file.

sections.title: Quickstart Validation Guide: Sales Item Management System
sections.raw_content: This guide describes how to verify that the feature is implemented correctly.

sections.title: Prerequisites
sections.raw_content:
- Modern Web Browser (Chrome, Firefox, Edge, or Safari).
- Project files served via a local server (e.g., VS Code Live Server) to avoid CORS issues with JS modules.

sections.title: 1. Catalog Display & Interaction
sections.raw_content:
- **Action**: Load `index.html`.
- **Expected Outcome**: 
    - A gallery of items is displayed.
    - Clicking an item opens a modal with full details and a larger image.
    - Closing the modal returns the user to the gallery.

sections.title: 2. Search & Filtering
sections.raw_content:
- **Action**: Enter a keyword in the search bar.
- **Expected Outcome**: The gallery updates in real-time to show only matching items.
- **Action**: Select a category from the filter dropdown.
- **Expected Outcome**: Only items of that category are displayed.
- **Action**: Toggle "Available Only".
- **Expected Outcome**: Items marked as `availability: false` disappear from the list.

sections.title: 3. Dynamic Sorting
sections.raw_content:
- **Action**: Change sort order to "Price: Low to High".
- **Expected Outcome**: Items are reordered instantly without page reload.

sections.title: 4. Item Management (CRUD)
sections.raw_content:
- **Action**: Open the management area $\rightarrow$ Add a new item $\rightarrow$ Submit.
- **Expected Outcome**: The item appears in the gallery immediately.
- **Action**: Edit an existing item's price $\rightarrow$ Save.
- **Expected Outcome**: The updated price is reflected in the gallery.
- **Action**: Delete an item.
- **Expected Outcome**: The item is removed from the gallery.

sections.title: 5. Persistence Check
sections.raw_content:
- **Action**: Add an item $\rightarrow$ Refresh the page.
- **Expected Outcome**: The added item is still present in the gallery.

sections.title: Validation Commands
sections.raw_content:
Since this is a vanilla JS project, validation is performed manually in the browser.
1. Start Live Server on `index.html`.
2. Open Browser $\rightarrow$ `http://127.0.0.1:5500/index.html`.
3. Execute the scenarios above.

elements.content: Must be compatible with modern web browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Edge, or Safari).
Project files must be served via a local server to avoid CORS issues with JS modules.
System shall display a gallery of items when loading index.html.
Clicking an item opens a modal with full details and a larger image.
Closing the modal returns the user to the gallery.
System shall update the gallery in real-time to show only items matching a keyword entered in the search bar.
System shall filter items by category when selected from the filter dropdown.
System shall hide items marked as availability: false when 'Available Only' is toggled.
System shall dynamically reorder items instantly without page reload when sort order is changed.
System shall allow adding a new item via the management area, which appears in the gallery immediately.
System shall allow editing an existing item's price, with updates reflected in the gallery.
System shall allow deleting an item, removing it from the gallery.
System shall persist added items such that they remain present after a page refresh.
Item entity contains attributes: image, details, category, availability, and price.

Explicitly define what features are in scope and out of scope for this project release.
Document any pending decisions, technical uncertainties, or open questions regarding the system.
